arxiv-1505-06533.title: Two-loop disorder effects on the nematic quantum criticality in d d -wave superconductors
arxiv-1505-06533.creator: Jing Wang
arxiv-1505-06533.description: Abstract The gapless nodal fermions exhibit non-Fermi liquid behaviors at the nematic quantum critical point that is supposed to exist in some d d -wave cuprate superconductors. This non-Fermi liquid state may be turned into a disorder-dominated diffusive metal if the fermions also couple to a disordered potential that generates a relevant perturbation in the sense of renormalization group theory.

arxiv-2205-09686.title: A new statistic on Dyck paths for counting 3-dimensional Catalan words
arxiv-2205-09686.creator: Kassie Archer, Christina Graves
arxiv-2205-09686.description: Abstract . A 3-dimensional Catalan word is a word on three letters so that the subword on any two letters is a Dyck path. For a given Dyck path D D , a recently defined statistic counts the number of Catalan words with the property that any subword on two letters is exactly D D .

arxiv-2206-04974.title: A coupled generalized three-form dark energy model
arxiv-2206-04974.creator: Xin-He Meng
arxiv-2206-04974.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Xin-He Meng. A coupled dark energy model is considered, in which dark energy is represented by a generalized three-form field and dark matter by dust. By assuming the functions N N and I I in the model’s Lagrangian as two power-law functions of the three-form field, we obtain two fixed points of the autonomous system of evolution equations, consisting of a attractor and a tracking saddle point which can be used to alleviate the coincidence problem.

arxiv-2209-14712.title: A method for computing hadron–nucleus cross sections in fully active sampling calorimetric targets
arxiv-2209-14712.creator: Johnny Ho, David W. Schmitz
arxiv-2209-14712.description: Abstract Interaction cross section measurements in fixed-target scattering experiments are typically performed by measuring the attenuation of a beam of particles that is incident upon a target slab of material. A fully active sampling calorimeter, such as the time projection chamber, is a more voluminous target that can be treated as a series of smaller target slabs.

arxiv-2410-12549.title: Poincare field theory for massive particles
arxiv-2410-12549.creator: B. Sazdović
arxiv-2410-12549.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by B. Sazdović. There is ambitious pretension formulated by Weinberg [ 1 ] that any relativistic quantum theory will look at sufficiently low energy like a quantum field theory. It is based on the observation that for formulation of quantum field theory … much better starting point is Wigner’s definition of particles as representations of inhomogeneous Lorentz group [ 2 , 3 ] . [ 1 ] starts with particles and get to the field equations later.

arxiv-2504-15797.title: Bridging Bond Beyond Life: Designing VR Memorial Space with Stakeholder Collaboration via Research through Design
arxiv-2504-15797.creator: Heejae Bae, Nayeong Kim, Sehee Lee, Tak Yeon Lee
arxiv-2504-15797.description: Abstract . The integration of digital technologies into memorialization practices offers opportunities to transcend physical and temporal limitations. However, designing personalized memorial spaces that address the diverse needs of the dying and the bereaved remains underexplored. Using a Research through Design (RtD) approach, we conducted a three-phase study: participatory design, VR memorial space development, and user testing.

arxiv-2504-21534.title: Topological classification and edge states of magnons in honeycomb ferromagnets
arxiv-2504-21534.creator: Youwen Wang, Qiutong Wang, Qingjun Tong, Ci Li
arxiv-2504-21534.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Youwen Wang, Qiutong Wang, Qingjun Tong, Ci Li. We study the topological classification and related edge states of magnons in ferromagnets on honeycomb that can be described by a class of single-particle bosonic Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) models. Both single layer and bilayer situations are considered.

arxiv-2507-01140.title: Multi-Focus Probes for Context-Preserving Network Exploration and Interaction in Immersive Analytics
arxiv-2507-01140.creator: Eric Zimmermann University of Rostock, Germany, Stefan Bruckner University of Rostock, Germany
arxiv-2507-01140.description: Abstract Immersive visualization of network data enables users to physically navigate and interact with complex structures, but managing transitions between detailed local (egocentric) views and global (exocentric) overviews remains a major challenge. We present a multi-focus probe technique for immersive environments that allows users to instantiate multiple egocentric subgraph views while maintaining persistent links to the global network context.

arxiv-2510-10429.title: Quantum-Resistant Cryptography via Universal Gröbner Bases
arxiv-2510-10429.creator: Sergio Da Silva, Aniya Stewart
arxiv-2510-10429.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Sergio Da Silva, Aniya Stewart. In this article, we explore the use of universal Gröbner bases in public-key cryptography by proposing a key establishment protocol that is resistant to quantum attacks. By utilizing a universal Gröbner basis 𝒰 I \mathcal{U}_{I} of a polynomial ideal I I as a private key, this protocol leverages the computational disparity between generating the universal Gröbner basis needed for decryption compared with the single Gröbner basis used for encryption.

arxiv-2512-09201.title: Residual Primitive Fitting of 3D Shapes with SuperFrusta
arxiv-2512-09201.creator: Aditya Ganeshan, Matheus Gadelha, Thibault Groueix, Zhiqin Chen, Vladimir Kim, Wang Yifan, Daniel Ritchie, Adobe Research
arxiv-2512-09201.description: Abstract We introduce a framework for converting 3D shapes into compact and editable assemblies of analytic primitives, directly addressing the persistent trade-off between reconstruction fidelity and parsimony. Our approach combines two key contributions: a novel primitive, termed SuperFrustum, and an iterative fitting algorithm, Residual Primitive Fitting (ResFit).

arxiv-2601-16534.title: Effective Field Theory Description of Light Dilaton
arxiv-2601-16534.creator: Qing-Hong Cao 1,2,3 , Jian-Nan Ding 3 , Bing-Hui Ge 4 , Hao Sun 5,6,7 , Jiang-Hao Yu 6,7,8,9
arxiv-2601-16534.description: Abstract Dilatons, the CP-even pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone bosons arising from spontaneous scale symmetry breaking, offer a compelling alternative to axion-like particles (ALPs) yet lack a comprehensive low-energy framework. We address this by constructing a systematic effective field theory (EFT) for the dilaton based on a manifestly scale-invariant regularization scheme.

arxiv-2602-04448.title: RASA: Routing-Aware Safety Alignment for Mixture-of-Experts Models
arxiv-2602-04448.creator: Jiacheng Liang, Yuhui Wang, Tanqiu Jiang, Ting Wang
arxiv-2602-04448.description: Abstract Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models introduce unique challenges for safety alignment due to their sparse routing mechanisms, which can enable degenerate optimization behaviors under standard full-parameter fine-tuning. In our preliminary experiments, we observe that naively applying full-parameter safety fine-tuning to MoE models can reduce attack success rates through routing or expert dominance effects, rather than by directly repairing Safety-Critical Experts.

britannica-1911-stirling-william-alexand.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-stirling-william-alexand.description: Article 'Stirling, William Alexander, Earl of (poet)' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 25), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. according to Drummond of Hawthornden, he was a student at the university of Leiden. He married, before 1604, Janet, daughter of Sir William Erskine, one of the Balgonie family.

europmc-pmc5007295.title: Microglia contact induces synapse formation in developing somatosensory cortex.
europmc-pmc5007295.creator: Miyamoto A, Wake H, Ishikawa AW, Eto K, Shibata K, Murakoshi H, Koizumi S, Moorhouse AJ, Yoshimura Y, Nabekura J.
europmc-pmc5007295.description: Microglia are the immune cells of the central nervous system that play important roles in brain pathologies. Microglia also help shape neuronal circuits during development, via phagocytosing weak synapses and regulating neurogenesis. Using in vivo multiphoton imaging of layer...

pmc-11198133.title: Discriminative Ability of Left Ventricular Strain in Mildly Reduced Ejection Fraction Heart Failure
pmc-11198133.creator: Fa-Po Chung, Tze-Fan Chao, An-Sheng Lee, Kuo-Tzu Sung, Wen-Hung Huang, Chih-Chung Hsiao, Cheng-Huang Su, Li-Tan Yang, Ying-Ju Chen, Yun-Yu Chen, Jo-Nan Liao, Charles Jia-Yin Hou, Hung-I Yeh, Chung-Lieh Hung
pmc-11198133.description: BackgroundLeft ventricular (LV) systolic strain is presumably a more sensitive myocardial indicator than LV ejection fraction (LVEF). Data regarding the use of LV strain in clinical risk stratification and in identifying angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor (ARNi) responders remain scarce in heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF).

pmc-11507577.title: The Effect of Lower Limb Combined Neuromuscular Electrical Stimulation on Skeletal Muscle Cross-Sectional Area and Inflammatory Signaling
pmc-11507577.creator: Amal Alharbi, Jia Li, Erika Womack, Matthew Farrow, Ceren Yarar-Fisher, Jivko V Stoyanov, Antimo Moretti
pmc-11507577.description: In individuals with a spinal cord injury (SCI), rapid skeletal muscle atrophy and metabolic dysfunction pose profound rehabilitation challenges, often resulting in substantial loss of muscle mass and function. This study evaluates the effect of combined neuromuscular electrical stimulation (Comb-NMES) on skeletal muscle cross-sectional area (CSA) and inflammatory signaling within the acute phase of SCI.

pmc-11510515.title: An Efficient Fabrication Approach for Multi-Cancer Responsive Chemoimmuno Co-Delivery Nanoparticles
pmc-11510515.creator: Jianxi Huang, Yu-Ting Chien, Qingxin Mu, Miqin Zhang, Petr Chytil
pmc-11510515.description: Background/Objectives: Cancer remains one of the leading causes of death, with breast, liver, and pancreatic cancers significantly contributing to this burden. Traditional treatments face issues including dose-limiting toxicity, drug resistance, and limited efficacy. Combining therapeutic agents can enhance effectiveness and reduce toxicity, but separate administration often leads to inefficiencies due to differing pharmacokinetics and biodistribution.

pmc-11690569.title: NAVIGATING THE PATH FROM PHD TO PI: INSIGHTS AND STRATEGIES FOR RESEARCH INDEPENDENCE
pmc-11690569.creator: Marissa Schafer
pmc-11690569.description: The path from PhD to PI can be a challenging uphill climb, and yet, there a are a multitude of steps one can take to increase the likelihood of securing an independent faculty research position. In this presentation, I will share insights from my path from PhD to PI.

pmc-12361727.title: Newly Identified Genetic Associations of Alzheimer Disease by Conditional Selective Inference: Potential Implications for the Tau Hypothesis
pmc-12361727.creator: Scott Hebert, Eric Nels Pederson, Zhengqing Ouyang
pmc-12361727.description: Over 6 million people are estimated to have been living with Alzheimer disease (AD) in 2020, with another 12 million living with Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI). Research has been conducted to evaluate genetic links to AD, but more research is needed to improve early disease detection and improve patient outcomes.

pmc-12409856.title: The predictive value of tacrolimus intrapatient variability and time in therapeutic range for renal transplant outcomes
pmc-12409856.creator: Ching-Yao Cheng, Hue-Yu Wang, Jaw-Horng Liou, Shang-Feng Tsai
pmc-12409856.description: BackgroundTacrolimus is key in renal transplantation. This study evaluated optimal intrapatient variability (IPV) and time in therapeutic range (TTR) thresholds and association with renal outcomes.MethodsThis single-center study (1999–2018) had a mean follow-up of 3 years. All patients received tacrolimus-based immunosuppression, and excluded those switching from cyclosporin.

pmc-12551245.title: Knowledge, attitude, and practice on mushroom poisoning among residents of Jilin province
pmc-12551245.creator: Xiuxian Zang, Wanling Xu, Dahai Xu, Lei Chen, Haixia Hu
pmc-12551245.description: BackgroundMushroom poisoning is a significant public health concern, with diverse species causing various degrees of toxicity. This study aimed to investigate the knowledge, attitude, and practice (KAP) towards mushroom poisoning among the population in Jilin Province.MethodsThis cross-sectional study was conducted among the general population in Jilin province between August 2023 and September 2023.

pmc-12662004.title: A comprehensive dataset of agarwood tree (Aquilaria Malaccensis) leaf images for disease analysis in Brunei Darussalam
pmc-12662004.creator: Wasswa Shafik, Rahayu Sukmaria Sukri, Chandratilak De Silva Liyanage, Nurul Hazlina Zaini, Soon Boon Yu, Mohammad Amiruddin Ruslan, Rosyzie Anna Awg Haji Mohd Apong, Ali Tufail
pmc-12662004.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The visual diagnosis based on foliar traits remains a cornerstone technique for the early identification of biotic stress, for instance, disease and pest infestations, in many economically valuable crops, including Aquilaria Malaccensis (agarwood). As a species of immense commercial and ecological significance, Aquilaria Malaccensis is particularly vulnerable to a range of pathogens and insect threats that can severely compromise resin production and tree viability.

pmc-12738512.title: Multiscale Theoretical Calculations Empower Robust Electric Double Layer Toward Highly Reversible Zinc Anode
pmc-12738512.creator: Yufan Xia, Zhen Luo, Shuang Chen, Yang Xiang, Gao Weng, Hongge Pan, Ben Bin Xu, Mi Yan, Yinzhu Jiang
pmc-12738512.description: Highlights A multiscale theoretical framework deciphers the molecular-ionic dynamics of the electric double layer (EDL) in aqueous rechargeable zinc batteries, correlating interfacial water aggregation, anion-specific adsorption, and electric field inhomogeneity to parasitic reactions and dendrite growth, thereby establishing EDL-driven design principles for ultra-stable Zn anodes.

pmc-12751441.title: Growth and physiological responses of Grammosciadium platycarpum seed treated with seaweed bio-stimulant under salinity stress
pmc-12751441.creator: Monib Lotfi, Ghasem Eghlima, Mohammad Hossein Mirjalili
pmc-12751441.description: Improving seed germination indices is one of the factors for achieving high yields in agriculture, which is affected by environmental stresses, especially salinity. Seed priming is one of the methods for improving seed germination parameters to cope with salinity stress. Seaweeds can maintain plant growth under stressful conditions due to their bioactive compounds, including hormones, vitamins, nutrients, and secondary metabolites.

pmc-13404205.title: Tailored conditioning for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in children with Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease: A tale of two pathways for IFN-γ and IL-12 defects
pmc-13404205.creator: Kavitha Ganesan, Minakshi Balwani, Nithya Seshadri, Vijayashree Muthukumar, Krithika Krishnakumar, Anuraag Nalla Reddy, Vidya Krishna, Indira Jayakumar, Ramya Uppuluri, Revathi Raj

pmc-13475818.title: Geospatial Discrepancy of Chronic Hepatitis B and Hepatitis D Testing in Alberta: A Population‐Based Spatial Analysis
pmc-13475818.creator: Bryce Tkachuk, Isabelle Couloigner, Carla S. Coffin, Jason Jiang, Stefania Bertazzon, Abdel‐Aziz Shaheen
pmc-13475818.description: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and hepatitis D virus (HDV) coinfection are major causes of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. The geographic distribution of CHB and alignment of anti‐HDV testing with CHB burden remain poorly defined. We aimed to examine if anti‐HDV testing and seropositivity align with areas of highest CHB burden.

pmc-13500376.title: Extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli with chromosomally integrated resistance genes isolated from a wild Asian black bear
pmc-13500376.creator: Michiyo SUGIYAMA, Tomoya MORIMOTO, Tetsuo ASAI
pmc-13500376.description: Carriage of antimicrobial-resistant bacteria in wildlife is a growing public health concern. We isolated an extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli from the feces of a wild bear collected in a persimmon orchard in 2025. The bear isolate exhibited resistance to ampicillin, cefazolin, cefotaxime, tetracycline, and chloramphenicol.

pmc-13679917.title: The Immunological Consequences of Pediatric Adenotonsillectomy: Myths, Evidence, and Unsolved Questions
pmc-13679917.creator: Barbara Verro, Gaetano Ottoveggio, Simona Fiumara, Carmelo Saraniti
pmc-13679917.description: Tonsillectomy is one of the most common surgical procedures in pediatric populations, indicated primarily for recurrent tonsillitis and upper airway obstruction. Palatine tonsils represent lymphoepithelial structures crucial for local and systemic immune surveillance, with a key role in lymphocyte maturation and the production of immunoglobulins, particularly secretory IgA.
